name: Ariad Two-Servo Robot V1
purpose: A small serviceable two-servo embodied-AI robot enclosure with two side-mounted rotating limbs and tool-less interlocking printed parts.

parts.name: Front body shell
parts.role: Protect electronics and establish the approved rounded exterior, camera face, tray latch windows, and service-panel guide channels.
parts.notes: Rear-open shell receives the tray and service panel without glue or printed-part fasteners; fit remains uncalibrated.

parts.name: Interlocking electronics tray
parts.role: Carry electronics, slide into the shell, and retain itself with print-plane cantilever latches and carrier dovetail rails.
parts.notes: Long planar snap arms follow the XY layers; 0.4 mm generic interface clearance requires a future coupon test.

parts.name: Slide-lock service panel
parts.role: Slide through shell guide channels and provide repeatable tool-less access through a releasable flex latch.
parts.notes: Printed flat on its broad face; latch cycle life and hand-release force are unverified.

parts.name: Left rotating limb
parts.role: Provide a rounded ground-contact surface through the left servo rotation envelope.
parts.notes: No self-righting or gait claim until simulation and physical tests.

parts.name: Right rotating limb
parts.role: Provide a rounded ground-contact surface through the right servo rotation envelope.
parts.notes: Mirrored assembly role; geometry may share a source only if interfaces remain unambiguous.

parts.name: Left keyed snap adapter
parts.role: Transmit servo torque through a keyed stem and retain tool-lessly in the left limb with compliant split fingers.
parts.notes: Printed-to-limb retention is provisional; the selected servo horn or spline may still require its manufacturer-specified hardware.

parts.name: Right keyed snap adapter
parts.role: Transmit servo torque through a keyed stem and retain tool-lessly in the right limb with compliant split fingers.
parts.notes: Printed-to-limb retention is provisional; the selected servo horn or spline may still require its manufacturer-specified hardware.

parts.name: Press-fit camera bezel
parts.role: Locate and protect the camera through a replaceable annular collar while providing the approved expressive eye treatment.
parts.notes: Printed flat on its broad face; optical field of view and retention force are unverified.

parts.name: Dovetail electronics carrier
parts.role: Slide onto tray dovetails and locate placeholder electronics with solid corner clips instead of screw posts.
parts.notes: Board dimensions, clip deflection, connector keep-outs, and removal force require measured components and coupon tests.

component_envelopes.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
component_envelopes.source: Planning placeholder; replace with an official mechanical drawing and the actual fitted-header envelope.

component_envelopes.name: Feetech SCS009 serial bus servo
component_envelopes.source: Feetech SCS009 V1.0 product specification. The 20T/4.8 mm spline is documented, but the supplied horn and printed adapter fit remain unverified.

component_envelopes.name: Small CSI camera module
component_envelopes.source: Planning placeholder; board, lens, ribbon bend, and field-of-view envelopes remain unverified.

component_envelopes.name: Single-cell battery
component_envelopes.source: Configurable placeholder; no battery has been selected or authorized.

interfaces.name: Snap-latched shell to tray
requirements: Tray slides from the rear and both printed-in-XY cantilever hooks remain externally releasable.
No glue or screw joins the printed shell and tray.
Latch force and cycle life require physical calibration.

interfaces.name: Slide-lock service panel
requirements: Panel guide tongues slide vertically and the top flex latch remains hand-releasable.
Power must remain off during service.
No adhesive or loose printed-part fastener is permitted.

interfaces.name: Left side rotary joint
interfaces.axis: Shared transverse X axis through the left body wall
requirements: Limb sweep must not collide with the body shell.
Adapter must be replaceable independently of the limb.

interfaces.name: Right side rotary joint
interfaces.axis: Shared transverse X axis through the right body wall
requirements: Limb sweep must not collide with the body shell.
Adapter must be replaceable independently of the limb.

interfaces.name: Camera and bezel stack
requirements: Lens and ribbon must not be compressed.
The shell and bezel must not obstruct the required field of view.

interfaces.name: Dovetail carrier to tray
requirements: Carrier slides along two open-ended 45-degree dovetail rails without screws.
USB, microSD, GPIO, camera ribbon, and power connections require service clearance.
The compute board must not carry structural servo loads.

interfaces.name: Battery restraint
requirements: Battery must not contact sharp edges or rotating hardware.
Battery swelling allowance and restraint material remain unresolved.

assembly_constraints: Exactly two independently actuated limbs are mounted outside the left and right body walls.
Every separately manufactured part receives its own geometry, printability, orientation, slice, and artifact records.
The complete assembly receives separate interface, collision, service-access, mass-property, and motion-simulation records.
No structural load may be routed through the camera or compute board.
The robot must remain serviceable without destructive adhesive on replaceable electronics.
Separately printed robot parts use tool-less slide, snap, press, or keyed-capture interfaces; selected purchased components may retain manufacturer-required hardware.
Hardware remains disconnected and physical success remains unclaimed.
unresolved_questions: Which exact servo and supplied horn will define the adapter interface?
Which battery format and protection board will be used?
Which camera module and lens field of view will be used?
What measured clearance coupon maps the generic 0.4 mm interlock allowance to the eventual printer, PETG batch, orientation, and elephant-foot compensation?
How many insertion and removal cycles can each PETG latch survive at the selected print orientation?
What mass distribution and limb length are required for simulated self-righting?
claim_boundary: This draft defines tool-less printed-part interfaces and generic FDM starting clearances. The servo envelope is manufacturer-sourced; the compute board, camera, and battery remain placeholders. Prototype CAD and disconnected slicer evidence do not prove interlock fit, latch life, component fit, collision freedom, motion, electrical safety, self-righting, or physical success.
